caveats: A same-key write is a supported hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. A duplicate widget key is not independently established to cause this exact exception.
The negative hypothetical reply moves directly to escalation without establishing that all other useful checks are exhausted.

question_review.question: Which Streamlit version are you running?
caveats: Knowing the version scopes investigation; it does not by itself establish that a bug is current, a regression or fixed. The reply overstates that determination.
The two hypothetical results are not clean alternatives: a currently installed release can itself be old. Their next steps need clearer version applicability.
The main-need wording groups slider with number_input although only number_input is reproduced. A clamp is bounded app advice, not verification of an internal product fix.

conclusion: The unchanged controlled-routing-v2 candidate produces 11/15 stored action matches (73.3%), versus 9/15 in the saved original policy-v3 full run. Answerable routing is 5/6, clarification is 3/6 and escalation is 3/3. The three actual questions are useful by assistant inspection with scope/next-step caveats. The main remaining action mismatches are DEV-5604, DEV-4338, DEV-3903 and DEV-3585; historical multi-part scope makes some alternatives defensible, so labels are preserved and ambiguity is reported. Content errors remain despite correct labels, especially incomplete workflow edits and unsupported causal/API interpretations. The identical-request annotation-case repeat drops a previously included persistent-stage correction. This is progress in stored-label agreement, not a verified 73.3% grounded-answer accuracy or a production-ready result. Keep the candidate experimental; no further paid calls or prompt changes are part of this run.
limitations: Adaptive development evaluation after repeated study/tuning on these same 15 cases; one new model sample each. Saved nonconcurrent original controls differ in prompt/schema/controller. No held-out, independent-human or application-runtime validation. Label agreement, question quality and grounded-answer completeness are separate.
